ai.description: *Ichthyophis davidi* is a caecilian reaching 28 cm. It is dark brown with a distinct yellow lateral stripe and a pale venter. Key features include a blunt snout and 280–300 primary annuli.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ichthyophis davidi* is best distinguished by its distinct, continuous yellow lateral stripe that extends from the head to the tip of the tail, unlike many regional congeners.
ai.habitat: *Ichthyophis davidi* inhabits moist, shaded areas within tropical evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found in damp soil near streams at mid-altitudes.
ai.behavior: *Ichthyophis davidi* is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to hunt for earthworms and other small invertebrates in moist soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ichthyophis davidi* is oviparous, laying clutches of 20–30 eggs in subterranean burrows near water. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ichthyophis davidi* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Ichthyophis davidi* consists of a series of short, high-pitched pulses, typically emitted by males while submerged in forest stream habitats.
